coordinates.note: No CERN geodetic-survey or metrology publication giving WGS84 coordinates for the underground LHCb cavern was found (checked 2026-09-17: the JINST detector paper could not be read because of bot detection and size limits; the LHCb Upgrade Framework TDR was checked only for bibliographic metadata; home.cern and lhcb-outreach.web.cern.ch state only the depth and the nearby village, not coordinates). The numeric lat/lon is an OpenStreetMap/Nominatim centroid for 'CERN Point 8', listed with the record's sources for provenance (the same method as for ATLAS Point 1) but not cited on this coordinate. It is a campus-grade point with large uncertainty, not a surveyed hall position.

depth.quote: It is 21 metres long, 10 metres high and 13 metres wide, and sits 100 metres below ground near the town of Ferney-Voltaire, France.

name: LHC Point 8 (LHCb)
notes: This is a NEW record, distinct from site:cern-lep-point-8-delphi (owned by historic-cern), which documents the same physical point during the LEP/DELPHI era. The two coexist and are not duplicates: they describe the same cavern at different eras with independently sourced facts.

The coordinate is a geocoder value, shown as a campus-grade point with large uncertainty; no primary or official source consulted (checked 2026-09-17) gives a detector-grade coordinate. See the coordinate note.

summary.plain: The underground cavern at Point 8 of the LHC ring, near the French town of Ferney-Voltaire, where the LHCb detector sits about 100 metres below ground.
summary.technical: LHC interaction point 8, Ferney-Voltaire (Ain, France); houses the LHCb forward-spectrometer detector approximately 100 m below the surface. Previously the site of the LEP-era DELPHI detector (see site:cern-lep-point-8-delphi).
